checks: Coverage makes R_i exactly the singleton region, since both other closed halfspaces are missed. A positive-area R_i contains an interior point of A with both strict inequalities; convex combinations with that point approximate every point of the closed intersection. Thus C_i is the asserted nonempty compact set.

In the pulled-back corner, the two threshold increments are t(b_j−v_j·p)+O(t²). At a proper cut, its chord interior lies in int A and only the two endpoints and the single crossing with the other line can affect pointwise convergence in the strip. Coarea gives precisely τ_ij with either inequality convention on the crossing point. It can be zero. The overlap of the strips is O(t²) by independence, with either sign of increments. Multiplying the retained corner by (1−t)² and subtracting from r_i gives D_i(p)=2r_i−Σ(b_j−v_j·p)τ_ij. Nesting implies D_i≥0 and the sign of the terms gives D_i≤2r_i on C_i.

In D_i the linear term is +p·Στ_ijv_j. Its minimum on C_i is the constant minus h_C_i(−Στ_ijv_j), so both support signs are as stated. The load bound holds on every singleton and on every multiple capture, hence integrates over one removed shell. Null corners have exactly zero measure there. The right side is affine with coefficient −Σ_i c_iΣ_{j≠i}τ_ijv_j, and its support maximum is attained on the same A, not by combining separate centers.

Independent check: take A=[0,1]², H_1={x+y≤3/2}, H_2={x≥3/5}, H_3={y≥7/10}. R_1 is a rectangle of area 21/50; the exact shell losses at p=(0,0) and (1,1) have derivatives 0 and 13/10, matching the formula even with negative threshold velocities. R_2 is a triangle of area 1/50 with D_2= (1−p_x)/5. With weights (1/10,1/10,4/5) the two deficient corners yield a common attained reserve 19/50 at (0,0), below the independent-minimum value 2/5; the two zero losses cannot be attained at one center.

With one positive-area deficient corner, 2aτ_2−2(τ_2−λ_j)r_j≥2τ_2(a−r_j). For the actual mixed weights τ_2≥Λ/4, giving (a−r_j)/2; r_j≤a/9 makes this ≥4a/9. If all deficient corners are null, 2aτ_2/Λ≥a/2. These are normalized weighted loss estimates, independent of a global below-2/9 depth assumption.
